name: beccs_capex_premium
description: Increase in total CAPEX for post-combustion capture and compression relative to BE at equal thermal input
notes: IEAGHG (2009) dedicated biomass CFB/BFB: +38-40% total investment (+114-126% per kWe net); range spans co-fired cases (+25-30%) to the upper end of Bhave et al. (2017).

name: beccs_eff_penalty
description: BECCS efficiency penalty (percentage points below BE)
notes: Mature (nth-of-a-kind) post-combustion amine capture at 90%: 7.7-11.9 pp for recent pulverised-coal studies, about 8 pp at Boundary Dam 3 (Herzog et al. 2016); 10.8 pp with present technology falling to 7.2 pp with improved solvents, compression and heat integration (Tramosljika et al. 2021). Lower bound: projected future penalties of 5.25-6.25 pp (Li et al. 2024). Upper bound: 2009 MEA technology on dedicated biomass plants, 12.8 pp (75 MWe BFB) and 15.9 pp (250 MWe CFB) (IEAGHG 2009).

name: capture_rate
description: BECCS CO2 capture efficiency
notes: Design basis of 90% capture in IEAGHG (2009) biomass CCS study and the literature on efficiency penalties (Herzog et al. 2016); 85-95% sampled.

name: ccs_distance
description: CCS transport distance

name: co2_pipeline_terrain_share
description: Fraction of CO2 pipeline CAPEX that scales with the route-average terrain cost multiplier (v2 transport layers)
notes: 1 = multiplier applies to all pipeline CAPEX, as terrain factors are usually quoted (IEA 2002); lower if unit costs already include a terrain allowance.

name: co2_subsea_capex_factor
description: Subsea CO2 pipeline CAPEX per km relative to onshore (offshore sinks reached by pipeline)
notes: Offshore pipelines typically cost 1.4-1.7x onshore per km. Keep equal to sea_route_weight_pipe in data-raw/process_transport_layers.R, which uses it to choose the landfall.

name: ccs_storage_cost
description: Onshore injection and monitoring (exploration to post-closure), for sinks without a site-specific cost
notes: Global CCS Institute (2025), 2024 USD: onshore US$2-15/t (open boundary), 5-33 (moderate closed), up to 58; ZEP (2011) onshore saline EUR 2-12/t.

name: cost_offshore_storage
description: Offshore injection and monitoring (exploration to post-closure), for sinks without a site-specific cost
notes: Global CCS Institute (2025), 2024 USD: offshore US$5-31/t (open boundary), 8-50 (moderate closed), up to 147; ZEP (2011) offshore saline EUR 6-20/t.

name: storage_cost_factor
description: Multiplier on site-specific CO2 storage costs (classified sinks in co2_sinks)
notes: Sinks with a site-specific cost (NETL formation cost for US onshore saline; GCCSI open or closed saline; ZEP depleted field) use Storage_Cost in co2_sinks x this factor. Range spans the NETL all-optimistic / all-pessimistic sensitivity (0.74-1.35 for Mount Simon, 0.57-1.71 for Copper Ridge) and most of the GCCSI and ZEP within-class ranges (issue #103).

name: co2_pipe_capex_km
description: Capital cost of a CO2 pipeline carrying 1 Tg/yr, per km (scaled by ccs_transport_location_factor)
notes: McCollum & Ogden (2006) UCD-ITS-RR-06-14: Ccap = 9970 m^0.35 L^0.13 $/km (2005 USD; m t/day, L km) = 0.47 M$/km at 1 Mt/yr over 100 km in 2024 USD (x1.606 CPI-U); Solomon et al. (2024) diameter regression (2.1575 EUR/m per mm + 0.018, 2024 EUR) gives 0.47-0.58 M$/km for the 200-250 mm needed for 1 Mt/yr. With exponent 0.5 the model matches NETL CO2_T_COM-based designs (PCOR 2022: 4.3, 10 and 20 Mt/yr) within 7%.

name: co2_pipe_scale_exp
description: Exponent of pipeline capital cost per km on CO2 flow
notes: Diameter scales with the square root of flow at a fixed economic velocity and cost per km roughly linearly with diameter (Solomon et al. 2024 regression) -> 0.5. McCollum & Ogden (2006): 0.35. NETL-based designs (PCOR 2022): upsizing 16 -> 30 in. raises capacity 5.9x for 2.2x cost (0.45). Pipeline cost sensitivity (issue #64): exponent 0.35-0.6 moves the takeover price by <= 5 US$/Mg.

name: co2_pipe_om_frac
description: Annual O&M of CO2 pipelines as a fraction of capital cost
notes: McCollum & Ogden (2006): 2.5%; Roussanaly et al. (2013) Int. J. Greenh. Gas Control 12, 341: 5% below 10 in. diameter, 3% at 10-26 in., 1% above. Plant feeders are below 10 in. and the 3 Mt/yr trunkline about 12-16 in.

name: co2_pipe_booster_km
description: Route length beyond which booster pumping raises the marginal pipeline capital cost
notes: With co2_pipe_booster_mult = 2, the average cost per km rises about 1.3x from 100 to 1,000 km, as the length exponent 0.13 of McCollum & Ogden (2006) implies (1.35x).

name: co2_pipe_booster_mult
description: Multiplier on the marginal pipeline capital cost beyond co2_pipe_booster_km
notes: See co2_pipe_booster_km.

name: co2_trunk_flow
description: Design flow of shared CO2 trunklines
notes: Design assumption of the hub-and-spoke network; the dedicated-pipeline variant tests it (fig-si-variants).

name: co2_feeder_km
description: Length of the dedicated feeder pipeline from each plant to the trunkline
notes: Design assumption of the hub-and-spoke network; the dedicated-pipeline variant tests it (fig-si-variants).

name: co2_ship_emis_fixed
description: CO2 emitted per tonne shipped, fixed part (liquefaction, loading, intermediate storage)
notes: From Al Baroudi et al. (2021): emissions of liquefaction and electricity are ~2.5% of CO2 transported at 200 km and ~18% at 12,000 km (fixed ~2.2% + 0.0013%/km).

name: co2_ship_emis_per_km
description: CO2 emitted per tonne shipped per km of voyage
notes: Al Baroudi et al. (2021); see co2_ship_emis_fixed. Pipeline lift pumping electricity is counted at the displaced grid intensity.

name: co2_liquefaction_cost
description: CO2 liquefaction for ship transport (scaled by ccs_transport_location_factor)
notes: Chen and Morosuk (2021): 21.13-21.3 USD/t (2021) for the least-cost processes at 15 bar / -30 C x 1.158 (CPI-U 2024/2021) (issue #87).

name: co2_ship_terminal_cost
description: Fixed ship transport cost per tonne: ships, buffer storage and terminals (scaled by ccs_transport_location_factor)
notes: ZEP (2011) The Costs of CO2 Transport, 2.5 Mtpa point-to-point ship case (Q2-2009 EUR): ship cost excluding liquefaction 8.2 EUR/t at 180 km to 14.5 at 1500 km, intercept ~7.3 EUR/t x 2.03 (1.39 USD/EUR 2009 x CPI-U 2024/2009 1.462) = ~15 (issue #87).

name: co2_ship_voyage_cost
description: CO2 ship voyage cost per tonne per km
notes: ZEP (2011), 2.5 Mtpa ship case: slope (14.5 - 8.2) / (1500 - 180) = 0.0048 EUR/t/km (Q2-2009) x 2.03 = ~0.010. Also sets sea_route_weight_ship in data-raw/process_transport_layers.R (voyage / 0.05 $/t/km trunk cost) (issue #87).

name: bes_capital_cost
description: Local CAPEX for BE at a 50 MWe reference plant (quoted at bes_capex_ref_eff); already regional, so capex_location_factor is not applied
notes: US: EIA AEO2026 (Sargent & Lundy) 50 MW wood BFB $4,843/kW 2025$ = ~4,720 (AEO2020: $4,097 2019$ = 5,030). Europe: Danish Energy Agency (2020) large straw CHP, 41.6 MWe, EUR 3.4M/MWe 2015 (range 2.9-4.0) = 4,990, ~4,720 scaled to 50 MWe; divided by 1.09 (DEA straw vs wood-chip CHP cost per MW fuel input, 80 MW feed plants) = ~4,330, because the base is a wood-fired plant and the ash penalty (adjust_costs_for_fuel) is added separately; cf. DEA medium wood-chip CHP scaled to 50 MWe ~4,110. China and India: IRENA (2025) weighted-average installed cost of bioenergy commissioned in 2024, 2,180 and 1,858 (2024 USD). India low end: CERC RE Tariff Regulations 2024 rice-straw Rankine norm Rs 697 lakh/MW = ~925/kWe net, so India's lower bound is 0.5 (950). Range otherwise x0.85-1.25, covering the DEA 2020 range and AEO2020.

name: bes_capex_ref_eff
description: Net electrical efficiency at which bes_capital_cost is quoted; sizes combustion CAPEX from thermal input
notes: Fixed design point, so sampled efficiency, ash and CCS penalties change output but not equipment cost.

name: bes_energy_efficiency
description: Electrical efficiency for BE
notes: Danish Energy Agency (2026), Technology Data for Electricity and District Heating Production: ~30% net electrical efficiency for biomass condensing plants.

name: bc_cl_retention
description: Fraction of feedstock chlorine retained in biochar
notes: Straw releases 60-70% of its Cl as HCl by 350 C (Saleh et al. 2014, Energy Fuels 28:3738) and 32-62% over 400-600 C; KCl evaporates only above about 700 C (Knudsen et al. 2004, Energy Fuels 18:1385). Released Cl raises the char ANC.

name: bc_s_retention
description: Fraction of feedstock sulphur retained in biochar
notes: About 60% of biomass S is released by 350 C (Saleh et al. 2014, Energy Fuels 28:3738); S release continues at higher temperature (Knudsen et al. 2004).

name: ash_cl_fly
description: Fraction of feedstock chlorine captured in combustion fly ash (as KCl)
notes: Straw-fired grate boilers: K, Cl and S are enriched in the fly ash; Avedøre straw fly ash is 53% KCl, 29% K2SO4, 9% calcium phosphate and 9% insoluble (Reuse of alkali from bio fly ash, ETDEWEB 20881741). The rest of the Cl leaves as HCl. Fly ash K is set by the Cl and S it binds; with these defaults fly ash is 15-18% of ash mass for wheat and maize residues and 8-9% for rice, consistent with 80/20 bottom/fly ash in Danish straw CHP plants and 7-15% fly ash for straw grate firing (IEA Bioenergy 2018).

name: ash_s_fly
description: Fraction of feedstock sulphur captured in combustion fly ash (as K2SO4)
notes: See ash_cl_fly. The rest of the S leaves as SO2, except ash_s_bottom.

name: ash_s_bottom
description: Fraction of feedstock sulphur retained in bottom ash (as sulphate)
notes: Author judgement; small effect on bottom-ash ANC.

name: ash_p_fly
description: Fraction of feedstock phosphorus reporting to fly ash
notes: Calcium phosphate is 9% of Avedøre straw fly ash (ETDEWEB 20881741); most P stays in the bottom ash.

name: fly_ash_recycled
description: Fraction of combustion fly ash returned to cropland
notes: Default 0: fly ash is landfilled because of its heavy metal content, while bottom ash is returned to fields (Danish practice). IEA Bioenergy (2018) estimates that nearly all Danish straw ash is used as fertiliser or soil improver, so the MC samples 0-1. Recycled fly ash is credited for its K and P; its ANC is negligible. Fly ash disposal cost is not charged separately: it is part of plant O&M (plant_om_factor), benchmarked to plants whose O&M includes ash handling and disposal, and is below US$1.5 per Mg feed.

name: ash_app_rate
description: Application rate of combustion ash to cropland
notes: Danish Bioash Order (BEK 732/2019): straw ash up to 5 t dry matter per ha per 5 years. Converts the per-hectare spreading cost and diesel (bc_spread_cost, bc_spread_diesel) to a cost per Mg ash.

name: lime_effectiveness
description: Effective share of the acid-neutralising capacity of biochar and ash
notes: ANC from the charge balance 2Ca + 2Mg + K + Na - Cl - 2S - P (residue_minerals()); silicate- and organic-anion-bound alkalinity counted in full. No evidence found to distinguish reactivity between pathways.

name: bc_ag_value
description: Biochar agronomic value

name: bc_price
description: Biochar price

name: bc_stab_factor
description: Biochar stability factor
notes: Validation needed: Ensure aligns with IPCC or verified carbon standard methodologies.

name: n_app_rate
description: Mineral N fertiliser application rate on cropland
notes: FAOSTAT N use per ha of cropland (via Our World in Data), 2019-2023 mean; default = world mean.

name: n2o_ef
description: Direct N2O emission factor for fertiliser N
notes: IPCC (2019) Refinement EF1 aggregated default and uncertainty range.

name: bc_dose_exponent
description: Exponent of the power-law crop yield response to the biochar stock (soils with pH >= 6.5)
notes: Meta-analysis of field trials in Woolf et al. (2016), Xu et al. (2021, Soil Tillage Res. 213, 105125) and Zhang et al. (2023, Sci. Total Environ. 905, 167290); docs/biochar_agronomy_handover. Within-experiment fit on soils with pH >= 6.5 (100 experiments, 50 studies), 90% CI 0.16-0.46. All field soils 0.50 (0.29-0.66); pH < 6.0 0.64 (liming adds a near-linear term, credited separately as avoided lime).

name: bc_yield_b0
description: Intercept of the yield amplitude model (log response ratio of crop yield at the reference stock)
notes: Meta-analysis of field trials in Woolf et al. (2016), Xu et al. (2021, Soil Tillage Res. 213, 105125) and Zhang et al. (2023, Sci. Total Environ. 905, 167290); docs/biochar_agronomy_handover. Multilevel meta-regression a10 = b0 + b_acid max(0, 6.5 - pH) + b_cec ln(CEC) (434 obs, 51 studies); b0 SE 0.0762. Normal: dist_min/dist_max are the 5th/95th percentiles. Sampled jointly with bc_yield_bcec (parameter_correlations.csv). The acid term (0.0696) is not used: the pH response is credited as avoided lime. Pessimistic case (pH >= 6.5 soils only, 19 studies): b0 0.2127, b_cec -0.0491.

name: bc_yield_bcec
description: Soil CEC slope of the yield amplitude model
notes: Meta-analysis of field trials in Woolf et al. (2016), Xu et al. (2021, Soil Tillage Res. 213, 105125) and Zhang et al. (2023, Sci. Total Environ. 905, 167290); docs/biochar_agronomy_handover. Coefficient of ln(CEC), SE 0.0252; response falls to zero at CEC = 36 cmolc/kg. Normal: dist_min/dist_max are the 5th/95th percentiles; correlation with bc_yield_b0 -0.870.

name: bc_yield_bref
description: Reference biochar stock of the yield amplitude model
notes: Dose to which field observations are normalised in the meta-analysis.

name: bc_yield_bmin
description: Smallest biochar stock on the power-law yield response (linear through the origin below)
notes: Few trials test smaller doses; extrapolating the power law below them implies unbounded yield benefit per Mg as the dose approaches zero. Sensitivity 1-5.

name: bc_yield_decay
description: Decline rate of the biochar crop yield response beyond biochar carbon loss (applied to the stock as bc_yield_decay / bc_dose_exponent)
notes: Response decline rate, as estimated from repeated measurements; the stock decays at this rate divided by the dose exponent so that a single application reproduces it. Persistence fit to 70 series (23 studies; median follow-up 1 yr): 0.14 yr-1 (90% CI -0.43 to 0.31, bootstrap over studies), -0.30 without Cornelissen et al. (2013), -0.36 on soils with pH >= 6.5 (37 series, 11 studies; negative whichever study is left out). Mode 0.05 (response half-life about 14 yr): persistence of the CEC component (Cheng et al. 2006; Liang et al. 2006) and of Anthrosol fertility (Glaser et al. 2001; Solomon et al. 2016), with slow decline from occlusion (Brodowski et al. 2006), translocation and erosion (Major et al. 2010; Rumpel et al. 2006) and transient first-year effects. Upper bound near the bootstrap 95th percentile, covering fading of single applications over 5-10 yr (Yang et al. 2025). Lower bound 0. Supplementary Text S3.

name: n2o_lnrr
description: Log response ratio of soil N2O emissions to biochar addition
notes: Meta-analysis of field trials in Woolf et al. (2016), Xu et al. (2021, Soil Tillage Res. 213, 105125) and Zhang et al. (2023, Sci. Total Environ. 905, 167290); docs/biochar_agronomy_handover. Multilevel random-effects model of clean field contrasts in Xu et al. (2021) (160 obs, 36 studies): -0.224, SE 0.068, i.e. a 20% reduction (90% CI 11-29%). No detectable dose dependence between 2.2 and 72 Mg/ha. Normal: dist_min/dist_max are the 5th/95th percentiles.

name: n2o_half_life
description: Half-life of the biochar N2O reduction after each application
notes: Central 2 yr: the reduction peaks about 1.5 yr after application and declines thereafter (Kaur et al. 2023, GCB Bioenergy 15, 24; evaluation of 18 meta-analyses) and diminishes after single applications (Yang et al. 2025, PNAS 122, e2509237122). Lower bound 1 yr: negligible after one year (Borchard et al. 2019, Sci. Total Environ. 651, 2354); vanished in the second year (Liu et al. 2020, Sci. Total Environ. 721, 137636). Upper bound 10 yr (about 60% of the reduction left after 7-8 yr): reductions persisting 7 yr after application (Guo et al. 2023, GCB Bioenergy 15, 478) and about 8 yr (Zhang et al. 2026, Agriculture 16, 433). Reversal of the effect with ageing (Song et al. 2016; Wang et al. 2024) is not modelled; see Discussion.

name: n2o_min_dose
description: Lowest biochar dose tested for the N2O reduction (reduction proportional to dose below it)
notes: Lowest dose in the field N2O data (Xu et al. 2021).

name: n_fert_replacement
description: Fertilizer replacement value of the N in retained residue
notes: Central 0: cereal residues have a high C:N ratio and immobilize soil mineral N as they decompose; subsequent crops recovered 4.5%, 2.7% and 1.1% of 15N-labelled straw N in three years (Thomsen & Jensen 1994, Agric. Ecosyst. Environ. 49, 115), gross of the fertilizer N immobilized meanwhile. Upper bound 0.1 covers that gross recovery and N-richer soybean residues (the residue composition is cereal-only). Charged only on the share not burned (residue_removal_charge()).

name: cropping_intensity
description: Cropping intensity (harvested area / physical cropland excluding fallow)
notes: Waha et al. (2020) Glob. Environ. Change 64, 102131: multiple cropping on 36% of cropland in China (Frolking et al. 2002: 38%), triple cropping 1.8-10.9%, so about 1.4; India 35-41% of cropland in national censuses (their gridded estimate, 16%, is an acknowledged underestimate), so about 1.4; multiple cropping is concentrated in East and South Asia and rare in North America and Europe (about 1). Excludes fallow (global 1.13 excluding, 0.82 including fallow). Converts residue and crop value per harvested hectare to per hectare of cropland.

name: bc_spread_cost
description: Cost of spreading biochar or ash, per hectare and pass
notes: Spreading share (70%, by the diesel use of a manure spreader, 14 L/ha, and power harrow, 6 L/ha; Leppakoski et al. 2021) of the combined spreading and incorporation cost of 116 $/ha (nets1.xlsm, Woolf et al. 2016; 87.8 in 2014 USD x 1.325). Range 0-163 = 0.7 x 0-233. Incorporation is not charged: application is timed to precede tillage (Claassen et al. 2018; Eurostat 2016; Dang et al. 2018). Scaled by field_ops_cost_factor.

name: bc_spread_diesel
description: Tractor diesel for spreading biochar or ash, per hectare and pass
notes: Spreading share (70%, by the diesel use of a manure spreader, 14 L/ha, and power harrow, 6 L/ha; Leppakoski et al. 2021) of the combined spreading and incorporation diesel median of 17.5 L/ha (Roberts et al. 2010 ~13; Cheng et al. 2025 ~15; Leppakoski et al. 2021 20; Pujol Pereira et al. 2016). Range = 0.7 x 13-30. Incorporation is not charged (see bc_spread_cost).

name: bc_horizon
description: Horizon over which the field effects of applied biochar are evaluated
notes: Biochar remains in the soil after the plant closes; same horizon as the permanence factor.

name: bc_dose_options
description: Biochar dose options per application (0 = annual application to all cropland)
notes: Each cell uses the option with the highest net value at the carbon price (biochar_field_table()).

name: max_residue_per_ha
description: Upper bound on available residue per harvested hectare
notes: Applied where the residue and harvested-area maps disagree (cells with residue but little harvested area). Total residue of double- or triple-cropped high-yield cereals is about 15-20 Mg DM per hectare of cropland per year.

name: us_base_cost
description: US farm-gate price of crop residues, excluding the grower payment for nutrients removed
notes: Perlack et al. (2011) Billion-Ton Update: $50 per dry short ton (2011) less the grower nutrient payment of about $26 per dry ton (Tables 4.2-4.3; 2006-2009 fertilizer prices) = $24 x 1.538 ($/dry ton 2011 -> 2024 $/Mg) = 37. Nutrient removal is charged in every region (residue_removal_charge()). Used for the US only.

name: price_k
description: Market price for potassium (world market; all regions)
notes: Potassium chloride 516 $/t / 0.60 kg K2O/kg. World Bank Commodity Price Data (Pink Sheet), annual nominal prices 2021-2025, each year escalated to 2024 USD with US CPI-U, then averaged. World market price used in all regions: retail subsidies (India) and export controls (China) are transfers that do not reduce the economic value of the fertilizer displaced.

name: price_lime
description: Cost of agricultural lime delivered and spread, per Mg of calcium carbonate equivalent (100% ECCE)
notes: Median of literature values incl. transport and application, converted to 100% ECCE and escalated with US CPI-U: Latawiec et al. (2019) Brazil 24.7 $/t delivered, no application (2018) = 31; Mills et al. (2020) Oklahoma (9.92 lime + 5.51 transport + 7.72 application) / 0.55 ECCE (2019) = 52 (Mills et al. 2023 use the same prices); Cho et al. (2020) Oklahoma 48 near / 90 far from quarry at 100% ECCE incl. application (2019) = 59 / 110; Woods et al. (2026) North Carolina 85 $/t spread (USDA, Dec 2024). Price years assumed one year before publication where not stated.

name: price_n
description: Market price for nitrogen (world market; all regions)
notes: Urea 486 $/t / 0.46 kg N/kg. World Bank Commodity Price Data (Pink Sheet), annual nominal prices 2021-2025, each year escalated to 2024 USD with US CPI-U, then averaged. World market price used in all regions: retail subsidies (India) and export controls (China) are transfers that do not reduce the economic value of the fertilizer displaced.

name: price_p
description: Market price for phosphorus (world market; all regions)
notes: Triple superphosphate 585 $/t / 0.46 kg P2O5/kg (a P-only fertilizer; DAP net of its N value gives 1.03). World Bank Commodity Price Data (Pink Sheet), annual nominal prices 2021-2025, each year escalated to 2024 USD with US CPI-U, then averaged. World market price used in all regions: retail subsidies (India) and export controls (China) are transfers that do not reduce the economic value of the fertilizer displaced.

name: py_cc
description: Pyrolysis unit capital cost in the United States (scaled by capex_location_factor), per Mg/yr of feed at the 50 MWe reference size
units: US$ per Mg yr^-1^ of feed capacity (2024 USD)
notes: NREL, Yadav & Lamers (2026) Energy Fuels 40, 4670, slow pyrolysis 2000 dry t/day, nth-plant TCI $128M (2020$) = 195 $/(t/yr) at 90% on-stream (657 kt/yr) = 236 (2024$, CPI-U x1.212), scaled with exponent 0.7 to the 206 kt/yr reference = 335. Other regions follow capex_location_factor (Europe 305, China 157, India 135). Caveat: NREL reactor at 300 C (model 500 C).

name: py_life
description: Pyrolysis project lifetime
notes: Woolf et al. (2016) Nature Communications (nets1 model).

name: bebcs_power_life
description: PyCCS power block lifetime
notes: Woolf et al. (2016) Nature Communications (nets1 model).

name: bebcs_heat_life
description: PyCCS heat block lifetime

name: bebcs_power_capital_cost
description: Pyrolysis vapour/gas combustion and steam power block capital cost in the United States (scaled by capex_location_factor)
notes: Between the steam cycle alone, 2,650 (Dutta et al. 2015, NREL/TP-5100-62455 / PNNL-23823, nth plant: steam system and power generation TIC $52.45M for 48.3 MWe x FCI/TIC 1.747 = 1,897 $/kWe 2011$, x1.395 CPI-U), and a complete 50 MW biomass plant including solid-fuel handling (4,700; EIA AEO2026); the midpoint of a 3,000-3,500 range allows for the vapour/gas combustor and boiler. Range 2,600-4,060 (US). Other regions follow capex_location_factor.

name: bebcs_heat_capital_cost
description: Syngas heat generation capital cost

name: bebcs_heat_efficiency
description: Heat-only block efficiency (heat sold / fuel LHV; heat sensitivity scenario)
notes: Biomass/syngas boiler for process heat; TODO(#106) source.

name: heat_price
description: No-carbon price of the displaced heat (fuel cost / boiler efficiency; heat sensitivity scenario)
notes: Exploratory, TODO(#106) source: US delivered industrial gas ~4.5 $/MMBtu / 0.9 = 17; EU TTF 2024 ~34 EUR/MWh / 0.9 = 41; China thermal coal ~850 CNY/t / 0.8 = 23; India domestic coal / 0.75 = 15.

name: heat_boiler_ci
description: Life-cycle intensity of the fossil boiler heat displaced (heat sensitivity scenario)
notes: Exploratory, TODO(#106) source: gas boiler (US, Europe) ~0.20 combustion + upstream / 0.9 = 0.25; coal boiler (China, India) ~0.34 / 0.8 + upstream = 0.45. Displaced heat intensity = min(boiler, MEF(P) / heat_pump_cop).

name: heat_pump_cop
description: Seasonal COP of the grid heat pump that displaced heat converges to as the grid decarbonises
notes: Typical air- or ground-source heat pump seasonal COP for low- and medium-temperature heat.

name: heat_offtake
description: Share of heat output sold (heat sensitivity scenario)
notes: 1 = year-round heat demand at the plant; the scenario is reported only conditionally on such demand existing.

name: py_temp
description: Peak pyrolysis temperature
notes: Modelling assumption: the medium pyrolysis temperature class (450-600 C) of Woolf et al. (2021) Environ. Sci. Technol. 55, 14795-14805 and IPCC (2019) Refinement Vol. 4 Ch. 2 Appendix 4. Sampled to represent imperfect temperature control and gradients within the reactor and particles; drives biochar yield and H:C (permanence) jointly.

name: py_heater_eff
description: Pyrolysis process heater efficiency (HHV basis)
notes: Woolf et al. (2014) Environ. Sci. Technol. 48, 6492-6499.

name: py_parasitic_power
description: Pyrolysis plant parasitic electricity demand
notes: Woolf et al. (2014) Environ. Sci. Technol. 48, 6492-6499.

name: py_exhaust_temp
description: Temperature of vapours and gases leaving heat recovery

name: bebcs_power_efficiency
description: Electrical efficiency of pyrolysis fuel power block (LHV basis)
notes: Woolf et al. (2014) Environ. Sci. Technol. 48, 6492-6499.

name: target_ph
description: Target agricultural soil pH

name: time_frame
description: Time horizon of pyC permanence

name: gj_to_mwh
description: Conversion factor from GJ to MWh

name: gwp_n2o
description: Global warming potential of N2O (100-yr)
notes: IPCC AR6.

name: gwp_ch4
description: Global warming potential of non-fossil CH4 (100-yr)
notes: IPCC AR6.

name: kg_to_mg
description: Conversion factor from kg to Mg

name: molar_ratio_co2_c
description: Molar ratio of CO2 to C

name: allow_eor
description: Allow Enhanced Oil Recovery

name: ash_recycling
description: Recycle BE/BECCS bottom ash to cropland (lime, P and K value)

name: bc_return_haul
description: Charge handling for returning biochar to fields as a backhaul in the feedstock trucks

name: py_e_source
description: Pyrolysis process energy source (fuel / biomass / biochar)

name: bc_valuation_method
description: Biochar valuation method

name: bm_ash
description: Biomass ash mass fraction
notes: Residue-weighted mean ash content of the available cereal residue (Phyllis2 crop medians; Karan et al. 2023 crop mix; data-raw/karan_residues/biochar_from_residues_v2.1.R). Rice straw and husk are 56% of the available cereal residue in China and 99% in India.

name: bm_ca
description: Calcium content of the feedstock (residue-weighted cereal mix)
notes: Residue-weighted mean of the available cereal residue in the region (Karan et al. 2023 supply with crop-weighted livestock use; data-raw/karan_residues/biochar_from_residues_v2.1.R), from Phyllis2 crop medians (data-raw/karan_residues/phyllis2_cereal_composition.R). Converted to the dry ash-free basis with bm_ash. MC range: author judgement from Phyllis2 interquartile ranges (e.g. wheat straw K 5.8-12.4 around 9.2 kg/Mg).

name: bm_c
description: Biomass carbon mass fraction
notes: Phyllis2 (TNO): cereal straws, corn stover and rice straw, dry ash-free basis.

name: residue_soil_ghg_penalty
description: Net soil GHG penalty of removing residues (forgone SOC minus avoided soil N2O)
notes: Default 0: McClelland et al. (2025) find the SOC gain and N2O increase from residue retention approximately cancel through 2100 in all regions studied except the Brazilian Cerrado. For sensitivity, a SOC-only penalty (no N2O offset) is bm_c x 0.11 x 44/12 = 0.19 (formerly residue_c_retention = 0.11).

name: residue_burn_fraction
description: Share of removed residues that would otherwise be burned in the field (regional fallback where residue_burn_map is absent)
notes: Superseded by the cell-level layer residue_burn_map (data-raw/generate_residue_burn_layer.R, issue #31): Smerald et al. (2023) cereal burnt / production share, 2017-2021, times SPAM cereal field residue C (Karan et al. 2023 inputs), divided by Karan et al. (2023) available residue C, capped at 1. Regional values are the biomass-weighted means of that layer. Earlier values: US 0.02 and China 0.10 (estimates), India 0.16 (Jain et al. 2014, share of all residues generated), Europe 0.01 (EU burning ban).

name: residue_burn_factor
description: Multiplier on the cell-level burnt share (residue_burn_map)
notes: Uncertainty in the burnt share: satellite fire products under-detect small field fires (e.g. Punjab), and burning of non-cereal residues is not counted; the product is capped at 1.

name: residue_burn_cf
description: Combustion factor for field burning of residues
notes: IPCC (2006) Vol. 4 Table 2.6.

name: residue_burn_ch4_ef
description: CH4 emission factor for field burning of residues
notes: IPCC (2006) Vol. 4 Table 2.5.

name: residue_burn_n2o_ef
description: N2O emission factor for field burning of residues
notes: IPCC (2006) Vol. 4 Table 2.5.

name: bm_h
description: Biomass hydrogen mass fraction (daf)

name: bm_h2o
description: Biomass moisture content

name: bm_lhv
description: Biomass lower heating value (dry ash-free)
notes: Phyllis2 (TNO): cereal straws, corn stover and rice straw, dry ash-free basis.

name: bm_transport_fixed
description: Fixed loading/handling cost
notes: Beach et al. (2012): loading and handling 4.59 $/dry t (2012 USD) x 1.366 (US CPI-U 2024/2012). Also charged per Mg of biochar returned to fields as a backhaul.

name: bm_transport_var
description: Variable trucking cost per km of one-way haul (includes the empty return)
notes: Searcy et al. (2007): truck distance-variable cost 0.12 $/Mg/km for straw and stover in 2006 USD; x1.556 (US CPI-U 2006 to 2024) = 0.187, rounded to 0.19 in 2024 USD. Check: US truck operating cost ~$1.4 per km travelled (ATRI 2024) / 18-20 t payload x 2 for the empty return = ~0.15 $/t per one-way km.

name: feedstock_storage_cost
description: Interim storage of seasonally harvested residues for year-round supply (about six months), US/EU basis; scaled by feedstock_storage_factor
notes: Literature spread (2024 USD/Mg, dry): Becerra-Perez et al. (2022) 3.1; Brechbill & Tyner (2008) 6.9; Beach et al. (2012) FASOMGHG 10.5 at 4.6 months, 11.1 at 6 months ($1.00 fixed + $4.59 in/out + $0.30/month per dry ton); Shackley et al. (2011) UK on-farm 18 (26 weeks at $0.50/t/week), purpose-built 31; Kung et al. (2013) 34 (storage and handling); Karras & Thran (2024) Germany ~42 (36.4% of supply cost at 6 months, 86% dm). Central 15 between the US farm-scale estimates and UK on-farm storage; range spans the literature. Regional values via feedstock_storage_factor (India 0.2: Saboo et al. 2025, CEEW). Ebadian et al. (2013): dedicated loading equipment at storage sites is costly (used 3-11% of the year).

name: india_feedstock_cost
description: Field-side price of baled paddy straw in India, dry basis (used for India only; other regions use calculate_regional_feedstock_cost() values)
notes: Sokhansanj et al. (2023) J. Sustain. Bioenergy Syst. 13, 57: baled straw $33.14/t dm (2023 USD) x 1.029 = 34. Range: Erenstein (2011) paddy straw Rs 0.31/kg (~2008) = ~12, where straw is burned, to fodder-market straw ~50: rice straw Rs 246/100 kg, Patna (Duncan et al. 2020); wheat residue Rs 332.5/quintal (Lopes et al. 2023); maize stover Rs 3,000/t (Varatharajan et al. 2022). Pant & Pant (2025): rice straw $40-60/t potential farmer income. Replaces Rs 1,600/t (trade news).

name: eu_nutrient_deduction
description: Replacement-fertilizer cost included in the S2Biom straw costs, subtracted from them
notes: S2Biom road-side costs of straw include fertilization to replace the nutrients removed (Dees et al. 2017, D1.8, section 2.1.3). Estimated as the European straw composition (N 6.24, P 0.88, K 8.71 kg/Mg dm) at World Bank 2012 annual prices (urea 398.6, TSP 462, KCl 465.4 US$/t): N 5.4 + P2O5 2.0 + K2O 8.2 = 15.6 US$ = 12.1 EUR (1.285 USD/EUR). Lower bound 7.9 EUR = P and K only. Application cost of the fertilizer (1.3-6.3% of supply cost; Karras & Thran 2024) is left in.

name: haul_time_share
description: Share of variable trucking cost that is time-based (driver wages and benefits; truck payments; insurance; permits)
notes: ATRI (2024) An Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking: 2024 Update (2023 cost per mile). Scaled by the travel-time factor haul_kt.

name: haul_fuel_share
description: Share of variable trucking cost that is fuel
notes: ATRI (2024). Scaled by road distance and climb (haul_kd x haul_g); the remainder (repairs; tyres; tolls) scales with road distance.

name: haul_driver_frac
description: Share of time-based trucking cost that is driver pay (wages and benefits); the rest is truck and trailer payments; insurance and permits
notes: ATRI (2024), 2023 costs per mile: driver wages 0.779 + benefits 0.192 = 0.971 of 1.462 $/mi time-based (truck/trailer payments 0.360; insurance 0.099; permits 0.032). Driver pay is scaled by labor_cost_ratio, the rest by truck_price_ratio.

name: labor_cost_ratio
description: Hourly cost of a truck or farm-machinery driver relative to the US
notes: US: BLS OES May 2024 heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers mean 26.92 $/h x 1.25 for benefits (ATRI 2024 benefits/wages 0.192/0.779) = 33.6 $/h. Europe 0.9: Eurostat (lc_lci_lev) 2024 labour cost in transport and storage (NACE H) 29.3 EUR/h = 31.7 $/h (1.082 $/EUR); lower bound 0.6 for drivers from lower-wage member states. China 0.094: CFLP (2025) truck driver survey, monthly income mostly 5,000-8,000 CNY (central 6,500), over a third working >= 12 h/day; 286 h/month = 22.7 CNY/h = 3.16 $/h (7.19 CNY/$). India 0.027: driver pay ~20,000 INR/month (15,000-35,000; entry-level and rural drivers to long-haul), 260 h/month = 0.92 $/h (83.7 INR/$). Approximate; ranges are wide.

name: truck_price_ratio
description: Price of a heavy truck (tractor and trailer) relative to the US; scales truck payments; insurance; permits and half of repairs
notes: US: new Class 8 tractor ~170,000 $ + trailer ~45,000 $. China 0.23: Sinotruk HOWO-A7 tractor 257,000-330,000 CNY + trailer ~60,000 CNY = ~350,000 CNY = 49,000 $. India 0.25: Tata tractor-trailer ~45 lakh INR = 54,000 $. Europe 1. Approximate; upper bounds allow for shorter vehicle lives and lower payloads of rural trucks.

name: diesel_price_ratio
description: Diesel price paid by hauliers relative to the US (excluding recoverable VAT)
notes: 2024 averages. US: EIA on-highway diesel 3.76 $/gal = 0.993 $/L. Europe 1.44: EU Weekly Oil Bulletin EU-27 weighted diesel ~1.60 EUR/L incl. VAT, /1.21 ex VAT x 1.082 = 1.43 $/L; lower bound for hauliers' excise refunds in some member states. China 0.96: NDRC-regulated retail 0# diesel ~7.6 CNY/L /1.13 VAT = 6.73 CNY/L = 0.94 $/L. India 1.08: retail ~90 INR/L (outside GST; no input credit) = 1.08 $/L.

name: haul_speed_ratio
description: Ratio of US to regional mean collection speed (the regional level of travel time per km)
notes: Implied mean speeds of least-time routes on the Weiss et al. (2020) friction surface for 125 MWth plants (data-raw/generate_logistics_layers.R, <region>_haul_factors_norm.csv): US 55.5, Europe 44.2, China 24.1, India 28.8 km/h. Scales the time-based share of trucking cost between regions; haul_kt redistributes it within each region.

name: haul_grade_ratio
description: Ratio of regional to US mean grade fuel factor (climb fuel)
notes: Biomass-weighted mean grade fuel factor (1 + climb fuel / flat-road fuel) at 125 MWth: US 1.138, Europe 1.340, China 1.321, India 1.142 (<region>_haul_factors_norm.csv). Scales the fuel share between regions; haul_g redistributes it within each region.

name: field_ops_cost_factor
description: Regional multiplier on field and handling operations: spreading biochar or ash, loading and handling of feedstock and biochar
notes: Ratio of regional to US custom-hire prices for comparable operations (US: Iowa Farm Custom Rate Survey 2025: small-grain combining 40 $/acre, liquid spraying 9 $/acre, dry bulk fertilizer 7.30 $/acre, tandem disk 18.50 $/acre, lime 8 $/t). Europe 1.4 (1.15-1.65): NAAC contractor price guide 2024-25 (UK; 1.278 $/GBP): combining cereals 116.36 GBP/ha (1.55), granular fertilizer spreading 15.87 GBP/ha (1.15), lime 7.75 GBP/t (1.24), disc harrowing 58.34 GBP/ha (1.63). China 1.6 (1.2-2.4): wheat machine harvest 60 CNY/mu (MARA 2022 survey; 1.5), drone spraying 225 CNY/ha incl. labor (Wang et al. 2022, Agriculture 12, 397; 1.6), plowing+sowing+harvest >120 CNY/mu in Henan (Qiu et al. 2021, China & World Economy 29, 99; >=1.6), rotary tillage 50 CNY/mu (MARA 2023 spring survey; 1.9-2.4). India 0.55 (0.45-0.65): custom-hire combine harvesting Rs 3,217-3,400/ha in Punjab, 2018-19 (Anchala & Sachdeva 2020, J. Agric. Dev. Policy 30, 145; 0.65); tractor land preparation ~Rs 1,800/ha (about 0.45). Source-year prices converted at that year's exchange rate and escalated with US CPI-U.

name: feedstock_storage_factor
description: Regional multiplier on interim storage of feedstock
notes: US and Europe 1 (feedstock_storage_cost from US and UK literature). India 0.2 (0.15-0.35): Saboo et al. (2025, CEEW), Punjab paddy-straw depots: infrastructure INR 250 (rectangular) to 400 (round bales) per tonne, operations INR 12 lakh/yr per 10,000 t (120 INR/t), land rent excluded; annualized about 2.5-3 $/Mg vs 15 $/Mg. China 0.5 (0.3-1.0): weakly sourced; reported construction cost of 10,000 t straw collection-and-storage centres of 3-4 M CNY plus operations, about 6-10 $/Mg.

name: lignin
description: Lignin fraction

name: transport_emissions_factor
description: Heavy-duty truck emissions
notes: GLEC Framework v3.1 (Smart Freight Centre 2024), Table 9, Europe: articulated truck 34-40 t GVW, diesel, average/mixed load (60% load factor, 17% empty running): 101 g CO2e/t-km well-to-wheel (78 tank-to-wheel).

name: bes_life
description: BE (and BECCS) plant lifetime
notes: Danish Energy Agency (2026), Technology Data for Electricity and District Heating Production: 25-year technical lifetime for biomass power and CHP plants.

name: c_price
description: Carbon abatement credit price

name: capacity_factor
description: Reference capacity factor: biomass collection-distance layers are built at this value, and it applies where no technology-specific value is set
notes: Technology-specific values: capacity_factor_bes_base, capacity_factor_bes_flex, capacity_factor_beccs, capacity_factor_bebcs. Each technology reads the distance layer at the plant size with the same annual biomass demand (attach_size_layers).

name: capacity_factor_bes_base
description: BE capacity factor in base-load operation
notes: BE is evaluated in base-load and flexible modes in the same run; each cell takes the mode with the higher net value (calculate_bes). Base load: firm low-carbon supply in decarbonised systems (Daggash et al. 2019; Ahlstrom et al. 2022 for systems with ample other flexibility at high CO2 charges). Upper bound below the 0.91 availability (DEA 2026).

name: capacity_factor_bes_flex
description: BE capacity factor in flexible (load-following) operation
notes: Flexible mode: biomass power supplying hours of high residual load in systems dominated by wind and solar (Johansson et al. 2019; Lehtveer and Emanuelsson 2021, about 3,900 full-load hours). Paired with bes_flex_price_capture.

name: bes_base_price_capture
description: Ratio of realised to time-averaged wholesale electricity price for BE in base-load operation
notes: Hourly day-ahead prices of 24-31 European markets (Ember, from ENTSO-E), 2024-2025 median across markets; plant runs the highest-priced hours of each day over the available hours (CF / 0.91 availability), with perfect foresight and no start-up or minimum-load constraints (data-raw/elec_prices/price_capture.R). Base load at CF 0.85: 1.05 (1.03-1.04 in 2015-2023).

name: bes_flex_price_capture
description: Ratio of realised to time-averaged wholesale electricity price for BE in flexible operation
notes: Hourly day-ahead prices of 24-31 European markets (Ember, from ENTSO-E), 2024-2025 median across markets; plant runs the highest-priced hours of each day over the available hours (CF / 0.91 availability), with perfect foresight and no start-up or minimum-load constraints (data-raw/elec_prices/price_capture.R). Flexible at CF 0.45: 1.30 (p10-p90 1.19-1.42), up from 1.15-1.21 in 2015-2023 as solar grew. Upper end bounded by battery arbitrage: charging price / efficiency + levelised cost of storage (Ember 2025: 65 $/MWh) gives about 1.34 x average in Europe; seasonal scarcity, which batteries cannot shift but stored biomass can, may widen spreads (Geis et al. 2025). Lower end allows for start-up and minimum-load constraints. Ratios are European; applied to all regions as an assumption (issue #107).

name: capacity_factor_beccs
description: BECCS capacity factor
notes: Base-load operation is incentivised by high capital cost, CO2 removal revenue per tonne captured and steady-state operation of the capture plant, dense-phase pipeline and injection: 0.85 is the design target of CCS power plants (Petra Nova; DOE final report 2020); Boundary Dam 3 capture plant reached 94% availability in 2018. Most future-system models run BECCS near base load (Johansson et al. 2019; Prado et al. 2023); the lower bound reflects about 3,900 full-load hours where scarce biomass is directed to high-price hours (Lehtveer and Emanuelsson 2021). Upper bound below the 0.91 availability (DEA 2026).

name: capacity_factor_bebcs
description: PyCCS capacity factor
notes: Electricity is a small share of PyCCS revenue, so operation is limited by pyrolysis availability and continuity of biomass supply rather than by dispatch. NREL nth-plant pyrolysis designs assume 90% on-stream (7,884 h/yr; Dutta et al. 2015); the central value allows for interruptions of feedstock supply.

name: discount_rate
description: Cost of capital (real, after-tax WACC for bioenergy projects)
notes: Hatton et al. (2025) Sci. Data 12, 1912 bioenergy WACC projected for 2030 (nominal, post-tax, USD): US 8.2%, EU-27 mean 9.45%, China 8.9%, India 9.8%; converted to real with 2.5% expected USD inflation: (1 + n)/1.025 - 1. Real because all cash flows are in constant 2024 USD. After-tax (the common TEA convention); a pre-tax gross-up at statutory corporate tax rates (Tax Foundation 2024) would give 8.3/9.3/9.1/11.2% but overstates the effective tax wedge, which depreciation allowances reduce. Default = US.

name: capex_location_factor
description: Regional multiplier on plant CAPEX quoted for the United States (pyrolysis unit and PyCCS power block); not applied to BE/BECCS, whose CAPEX is set regionally, or to CO2 transport (ccs_transport_location_factor)
notes: Ratio of regional to US BE plant CAPEX (bes_capital_cost: 4300, 2200 and 1900 vs 4700 US$/kWe; EIA AEO2026, DEA 2020, IRENA 2025), so that PyCCS and BE/BECCS plants are costed on the same regional basis. Not sampled separately: py_cc and bebcs_power_capital_cost carry relative ranges. Chemical-plant location factors (Towler & Sinnott 2022, Table 7.7: China indigenous 0.61, imported 1.12; India 1.02; Western Europe 1.02-1.19, relative to the US Gulf Coast) were not used: they are based on 2003 data (Aspen Richardson manual), need updating for exchange rates, and the plant types behind them are not documented.

name: ccs_transport_location_factor
description: Regional multiplier on CO2 transport CAPEX (pipelines, booster pumps, liquefaction, ships and terminals)
notes: US and Europe 1: pipeline costs (co2_pipe_capex_km) are benchmarked against US and European studies. China 0.67: Liu & Gallagher (2011) IJGGC 5, 798, China-specific engineering-economic model; levelized onshore pipeline costs about two-thirds of developed-country estimates. India assumed equal to China (no India-specific source). Range 0.56-1.0 for China and India.

name: plant_om_factor
description: Annual O&M (fixed + variable) as a fraction of total CAPEX, for all conversion plants (BE, BECCS, pyrolysis, PyCCS energy block)
notes: EIA AEO2023 50 MW biomass: fixed $141.5/kW-yr + $5.44/MWh = 3.6%/yr at 85% capacity factor; IRENA (2012) stoker/BFB/CFB boilers: fixed 3.2-4.2% + $3.8-4.7/MWh; Danish Energy Agency technology data, 80 MW feed CHP: straw 4.4%, wood pellets 4.6%/yr all-in.

name: om_location_factor
description: Regional multiplier on the O&M-to-CAPEX fraction
notes: 1 everywhere: regional CAPEX already scales O&M in absolute terms. Evidence: EIA AEO2026 and DEA (2020) all-in O&M ~4.1% of CAPEX/yr; CERC (India, 2024) O&M Rs 54.7 lakh/MW/yr = 7.8% of its normative CAPEX, so lower labour cost does not lower the O&M-to-CAPEX ratio.

name: elec_price
description: Wholesale electricity price received by the plant (scalar fallback; spatial runs use the regional price layer)
notes: Spatial runs use data-raw/generate_elec_price_layer.R: wholesale (day-ahead or hub) prices averaged over 2023-2025, from EIA STEO hub prices (US), Ember/ENTSO-E day-ahead prices (Europe), provincial coal benchmark tariffs excl. VAT (China) and IEX day-ahead prices (India). The Monte Carlo range is applied as a multiplier on the layer.

name: ff_c_intensity
description: Displaced grid carbon intensity at today's effective carbon price (empirical build margin, IPCC life-cycle, biomass = 0)
notes: Spatial layer (generate_marginal_ci.R); scaled by MEF(P) at the scenario carbon price.

name: grid_p_now
description: Current explicit carbon price on power-sector emissions (MEF(P) anchor)
notes: 2024 averages: EU ETS EUR 65/t x 1.08 USD/EUR = 70; China national ETS CNY 98/t / 7.20 CNY/USD = 14; no national price in the US or India. The TEA carbon price is an explicit price.

name: mef_floor
description: Residual life-cycle intensity of a decarbonised grid (MEF(P) floor)
notes: Pehl et al. (2017): 2050 life-cycle emissions of nuclear, wind and solar 3.5-12 g/kWh; fossil CCS 78-110 g/kWh.

name: mef_draw_u
description: Selects a bootstrap draw of the MEF(P) curve (0 = central fit)
notes: Monte Carlo: uniform on (0, 1] picks one of 1,000 precomputed bootstrap draws (inst/extdata/mef_shape_draws.csv).

description: Flat carbon intensity value

name: plant_sizes_mw_th
description: Available plant sizes

name: rebound
description: Rebound effect

name: scaling_factor
description: Capital cost scale exponent

name: avg_dist
description: Average collection distance

name: collection_radius
description: Collection radius

name: dist_offshore
description: Distance to offshore sink

name: dist_onshore
description: Distance to onshore sink

name: dist_sink_km
description: Distance to EOR sink

name: dist_sink_saline_km
description: Distance to saline sink

name: feedstock_cost
description: Feedstock purchase cost

name: soil_cec
description: Cation Exchange Capacity

name: soil_ph
description: Native topsoil pH

name: soil_temp
description: Mean annual soil temperature

name: tortuosity
description: Ratio of road-path to straight-line haul distance
notes: Biomass-weighted mean circuity of least-time truck routes from fields to plant on the Weiss et al. (2020) motorized friction surface, for 125 MWth plants (data-raw/generate_logistics_layers.R, <region>_haul_factors_norm.csv); varies by no more than 3% between 50 and 250 MWth. Sets the regional level of road distance; the haul_kd layers redistribute it within the region.

name: plant_mw_th
description: Target plant thermal capacity
